title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover pager to reduce fragmentation and paging overhead
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory utilization and reduces spikey tail-latencies by introducing an adaptive eviction heuristic, fragmentation-aware allocator tweaks, and a host-spillover pager. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: High memory fragmentation and reactive paging in the KV cache has caused recurring tail-latency spikes under mixed-length workloads. Customers running long-context chat workloads observed abrupt OOMs or heavy host throttling when GPU memory fragmented and the previous eviction strategy aggressively evicted hot prefixes. This PR introduces an adaptive eviction heuristic (segment-aware LRU), a background compaction/auto-compaction path, and a lightweight spillover pager to host memory for cold segments to reduce paging thrash.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Implemented segment-aware adaptive eviction: the cache is partitioned into sticky segments (hot/warm/cold) and eviction probability is adjusted by segment heat and fragmentation score. This reduces evicting hot KV entries during bursty traffic.
- Added a fragmentation-aware allocator that tracks free-run fragmentation and triggers targeted compaction rather than full-scale defragmentation. Compaction runs asynchronously and is I/O- and SLO-aware.
- Introduced a host spillover pager: cold segments that exceed a fragmentation threshold are paged to pinned host memory via a lock-free spill path (pager) with a compact on-demand restore. The pager supports batching of restores to amortize PCIe round-trips.
- Scheduler integration: compaction/paging work is scheduled with a new backoff policy so heavy compaction does not contend with serving threads. A fast-path avoids compaction for sub-128 token KV hits to keep generation latency stable.
- Telemetry and safety: added metrics for fragmentation_score, spill_count, restore_latency, compaction_time, and eviction_decisions. Added knobs for max_spill_bytes_per_gpu and compaction_qps.
- Tests and benchmarks: added unit tests for concurrent compaction and race conditions, integration tests for pager restores, and microbench harnesses reproducing production sequence-length distributions.

Commits (summary):
- 3d2a7b3: kv: add segment-aware metadata and heat scoring (core algorithm)
- b9c8f4e: allocator: fragmentation tracking and targeted compaction engine
- 7f1c12d: pager: host spillover implementation + restore batching primitives
- 9a0d5b1: scheduler: compaction/pager workqueue + backoff policy
- 4b2e6f0: tests: concurrent compaction unit tests and integration benchmarks

Files touched (high level):
- src/serving/kv_cache/eviction.rs (algorithms and heuristics)
- src/serving/kv_cache/allocator.rs (fragmentation tracking, free-run metadata)
- src/serving/kv_cache/pager.rs (spill/restore paths, batching)
- src/serving/scheduler/compaction_scheduler.rs (workqueue, backoff)
- src/serving/kv_cache/metrics.rs (new metrics and labels)
- tests/kv_cache_eviction_test.rs (unit tests for concurrency and races)
- benches/kv_pager_bench.rs (microbench harness)
- docs/eviction.md (design notes and tuning guidance)

Testing and CI:
- CI initially failed lint (line-length) and a flaky unit test on macOS due to a race in the old test harness. Fixed lint and hardened the test; rerun CI passed all checks (build, fmt, clippy, unit/integration tests, bench smoke). The bench CI job is gated and ran separately.

Performance results (lab, representative):
- Fragmentation score (avg) reduced from 0.42 -> 0.18 on mixed-length chat workload (seq distribution 32/512/4096).
- Memory overhead reduced ~22% (measured as resident GPU memory used for KV vs baseline).
- Tail latency (p99 gen latency) improvement: 12-18% reduction in scenarios with high context churn.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~7% in steady-state due to fewer reactive evictions and less PCIe thrash from paging.
- Pager restore median latency: 1.8ms (batched restores) vs naive copy path 6.2ms.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- No public API or wire-protocol changes. All new behavior gated behind config flags (default to safe conservative thresholds). Rolling deploy tested with canary: small percentage of requests routed to the new eviction path before full enablement.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ben Torres (reviewer): "Nice work; the segmentation idea looks promising. Can you add an explicit unit test to show that hot entries are not evicted during bursts? Also please document the config knobs and expected defaults."
- Aisha (author): "Added kv_cache_eviction_hot_entry_test and expanded docs/eviction.md with recommended defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers."
- Marta Ivanova (reviewer): "We saw a small regression in the compaction_time metric during sustained write-heavy benchmarks. Can compaction be rate-limited further or moved to lower priority?"
- Aisha: "Scheduler backoff added in second patch to limit compaction QPS under sustained load; compaction now yields to serving threads and respects max_compaction_qps. Updated benchmark results included above."
- Jae Kim (approver): "Verified on a dedicated cluster with a long-chat sim harness. Approving after CI green and documentation added."

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main 2025-11-21. Rollout: feature gated; toggled on for Dedicated pools in canary region for 48h, then gradually enabled. Ops runbook updated with fragment/compaction alerts and recommended mitigation steps.

Related: ENG-1423 (KV memory stability epic), ENG-1499 (spillover pager work), SUP-789 (customer incident that motivated emergency investigation).
notes: Ops: monitor fragmentation_score and spill_count; recommended initial conservative defaults: max_spill_bytes_per_gpu=4GB, compaction_qps=20. See docs/eviction.md for tuning.
changelog_entry: Enhance KV cache eviction with adaptive segmentation, fragmentation-aware compaction and host spillover pager to reduce fragmentation, lower memory overhead, and improve p99 latency under mixed-length workloads.
